name: Abortion, Eugenic
description: Abortion performed because of possible fetal defects.

name: Abortion, Induced
description: Intentional removal of a fetus from the uterus by any of a number of techniques. (POPLINE, 1978)

name: Abortion, Legal
description: Termination of pregnancy under conditions allowed under local laws. (POPLINE Thesaurus, 1991)

name: Abortion, Therapeutic
description: Abortion induced to save the life or health of a pregnant woman. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: Dental Abutments
description: Natural teeth or teeth roots used as anchorage for a fixed or removable denture or other prosthesis (such as an implant) serving the same purpose.

name: Clinical Decision-Making
description: Process of formulating a diagnosis based on medical history and physical or mental examinations, and/or choosing an appropriate intervention.

name: Neurological Rehabilitation
description: Physician-supervised programs designed to rehabilitate people with diseases, trauma, or disorders of the NERVOUS SYSTEM.

name: Physical Appearance, Body
description: Externally visible physical characteristics of a body.

name: Direct-To-Consumer Screening and Testing
description: Laboratory testing and diagnostic imaging services offered to consumers outside of the patient-physician relationship.

name: Exoskeleton Device
description: Device designed to wear externally to support muscular skeletal system in various movements such as RANGE OF MOTIONS; WEIGHT-BEARING; GAIT; and LOCOMOTION.

name: Failure to Rescue, Health Care
description: Inability to prevent a clinical deterioration resulting from a complication of an underlying medical condition or a complication of medical care. It implies that common risk factors for such a complication were not recognized in a timely manner or treated appropriately.

name: Psychiatric Rehabilitation
description: Specialty field that promotes recovery, community functioning, and increased well-being of individuals diagnosed with mental disorders that impair their ability to live meaningful lives.

name: Isolated Heart Preparation
description: Method of isolation and maintenance of a working heart for various cardiac measurements. The model allows for the separation of cardiac and systemic variables in the denervated heart.

name: Diet, Vegan
description: Dietary practice of avoiding animal products in any form.

name: Behavior Observation Techniques
description: A wide range of formal and informal techniques used to document behavior.

name: Transanal Endoscopic Surgery
description: Surgical procedures performed through the anus using a PROCTOSCOPE.

name: Transanal Endoscopic Microsurgery
description: A specialized form of transanal endoscopic surgery for microscopically controlled operations in the RECTUM.

name: Personal Protective Equipment
description: Specialized clothing or equipment worn for protection against health hazards. Personal Protective Equipment may include MASKS; RESPIRATORY PROTECTIVE DEVICES; HEAD PROTECTIVE DEVICES; EYE PROTECTIVE DEVICES; EAR PROTECTIVE DEVICES; PROTECTIVE CLOTHING; and protective footwear.

name: Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale
description: A rating scale that measures INVOLUNTARY MOVEMENTS known as TARDIVE DYSKINESIA.

name: Cellular Reprogramming Techniques
description: Procedures used for the induction of CELLULAR REPROGRAMMING to change the terminal phenotype of a cell, such as the generation of INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS from differentiated adult cells by the forced expression of specific genes.

name: Near Miss, Healthcare
description: Event that presented a risk but did not result in a patient harm.

name: RNAi Therapeutics
description: A form of disease treatment which involves the silencing of genes that are associated with a disease by the process of RNA INTERFERENCE.

name: Dynamic Light Scattering
description: An analytical technique for measuring particle size of molecules that are less than a micron in diameter dispersed or dissolved in a liquid.

name: Healthcare Failure Mode and Effect Analysis
description: Prospective risk assessment tool aimed at identifying potential risks and their impact in healthcare settings.

name: Action Spectrum
description: A technique used to measure the rate of physiological activity plotted against wavelength of light. An action spectrum depicts the most effective wavelength of light (also known as spectral sensitivity) that is required for each specific process.

name: Surgical Clearance
description: Process of evaluating the health of a patient and determining if they are healthy enough for surgery.

name: Clinical Studies as Topic
description: Works about research studies that evaluate interventions or exposures on biomedical or health-related outcomes. The two main types of clinical studies are interventional studies (clinical trials) and observational studies.

name: Data Accuracy
description: A measure of scientific precision, exactness, or correctness of quantitative or qualitative values, relative to the actual or true measurements.

name: Selective Breeding
description: A process in which offspring possessing desired genetic traits are produced.

name: Spatial Regression
description: Methods used to take into account and incorporate spatial autocorrelation and regional variation into regression analysis models of data that has spatial dependency, and also to provide information on the spatial relationships among the variables.

name: Theranostic Nanomedicine
description: An integrated nano-scale approach to MEDICINE which involves concurrent diagnosis, drug delivery, therapy, and monitoring of therapeutic response.

name: Prisoner Dilemma
description: A scenario in decision analysis in which two individuals motivated entirely by self-preservation at the expense of the other, end up in a worse state than if they had cooperated with each other in the decision-making process.

name: Humidifiers
description: Machines that add moisture to the air.

name: Health Smart Cards
description: Hand-sized cards with built-in computer chips used for accessing, storing, and protecting patients' medical information.

name: Contraceptive Prevalence Surveys
description: Collections of data, obtained from voluntary subjects, that measure the usage rate of methods of CONTRACEPTION; CONTRACEPTIVE DEVICES; or CONTRACEPTIVE AGENTS.

name: Arthrocentesis
description: Puncture and aspiration of fluid (e.g., SYNOVIAL FLUID) from a joint cavity. It is used sometimes to irrigate or administer drugs into a joint cavity.

name: Thoracentesis
description: Aspiration of fluid or air from the THORACIC CAVITY. It is coupled sometimes with the administration of drugs into the PLEURAL CAVITY.

name: Arterial Switch Operation
description: Surgical procedure for anatomical correction of transposed great arteries (e.g., DOUBLE OUTLET RIGHT VENTRICLE).

name: Electrocorticography
description: Recording of brain electrical activities in which the electrodes are placed directly on the CEREBRAL CORTEX.

name: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy
description: In vitro fertilization technique that uses mitochondrial DNA from a healthy donor in order to prevent the transmission of MITOCHONDRIAL DISEASE.

name: Self Expandable Metallic Stents
description: Cylindrical metallic tubes that are inserted to hold open a structure in order to treat vascular, bile duct, esophageal and other tubular organ constrictions.

name: Trachelectomy
description: Surgical removal or resection of the CERVIX UTERI.

name: Deprescriptions
description: Directions written to discontinue use of PRESCRIPTION DRUGS in order to reduce unnecessary and/or excessive medications (see POLYPHARMACY), DRUG SIDE EFFECTS and ADVERSE DRUG REACTION.

name: Transitional Care
description: Health care provided during a transition to a different mode of care (e.g., TRANSITION TO ADULT CARE).

name: Bone-Implant Interface
description: Region of interaction between the bone and PROSTHESES AND IMPLANTS which becomes bonded through cellular and extracellular interactions similar to OSSEOINTEGRATION.

name: Telerehabilitation
description: Delivery of therapeutic rehabilitation at a distance or offsite using telecommunication technologies.

name: Tympanocentesis
description: Needle aspiration of fluid from the MIDDLE EAR through a puncture in the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE.

name: Intravital Microscopy
description: Type of microscopy used to study biological systems at high resolution.

name: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation
description: Transfer of GASTROINTESTINAL MICROBIOTA from one individual to another by infusion of donor FECES to the upper or lower GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT of the recipient.

name: Radiation Dose Hypofractionation
description: A treatment schedule in which the total dose of radiation is divided into large doses but fewer exposure times.

name: Re-Irradiation
description: Treatment in which a repeat course of RADIOTHERAPY is administered.

name: Injection, Intratympanic
description: The administration of liquid substances into the TYMPANIC CAVITY with a hypodermic syringe.

name: Morcellation
description: Use of a non-cautery–dependent mechanical device that simultaneously cuts and aspirates polyp and/or myoma tissue.

name: Endoscopic Mucosal Resection
description: A method for removing lesions from gastrointestinal MUCOUS MEMBRANES. The mucosal tissue with the lesion is elevated by injecting a solution into the submucosal layer underneath it. The elevated tissue with the lesion is then cut out.

name: Heart Rate Determination
description: Methods, techniques, and processes by which HEART RATE is measured.

name: Kinanthropometry
description: A measure of human size, shape, proportion, composition, maturation, and gross function; in relation to body movement, physical exercise, fitness, and performance.

name: Diet, Carbohydrate Loading
description: A diet rich in DIETARY CARBOHYDRATES.

name: Cystography
description: Radiography of the URINARY BLADDER.

name: Closed Fracture Reduction
description: A procedure in which normal alignment of a fractured bone is restored by ORTHOPEDIC MANIPULATION without incision.

name: Punctal Plugs
description: Small devices that are inserted into the tear ducts (NASOLACRIMAL DUCTS). They are used to block the drainage of TEARS for the treatment of DRY EYE SYNDROMES.

name: Ulnar Collateral Ligament Reconstruction
description: Surgical reconstruction of injured or insufficient ULNAR COLLATERAL LIGAMENT in the ELBOW JOINT.

name: Open Fracture Reduction
description: Restoration of normal alignment of a fractured bone via an OPERATIVE SURGICAL PROCEDURE.

name: Walk Test
description: A measure of endurance tests that show how far and fast an individual can walk without stopping within a certain period of time.

name: Phage Therapy
description: Therapeutic use of BACTERIOPHAGES to treat diseases.

name: Breast Density
description: Measurement of relative composition of different BREAST tissue types often determined from MAMMOGRAPHY; ULTRASONOGRAPHY; or MRI.

name: Traditional Pulse Diagnosis
description: Technique used in AYURVEDIC MEDICINE, and EAST ASIAN TRADITIONAL MEDICINE, in which reading PULSE is used in the diagnosis of diseases.

name: Sutureless Surgical Procedures
description: Surgical techniques in which SUTURES are not applied to surgical wounds.

name: Standing Orders
description: Medical procedures and prescriptions regarding treatment of a patient that can be exercised by other health care personnel when predetermined conditions have been met.

name: Patient Reported Outcome Measures
description: Assessment of the quality and effectiveness of health care as measured and directly reported by the patient.

name: Network Meta-Analysis as Topic
description: Works about meta-analyses of randomized trials in which estimates of comparative treatment effects are visualized and interpreted from a network of interventions that may or may not have been evaluated directly against each other. Common considerations in network meta-analysis include conceptual and statistical heterogeneity and incoherence.

name: Single-Balloon Enteroscopy
description: A balloon-assisted enteroscopy utilizing a flexible endoscope with one overtube balloon control unit.

name: Balloon Enteroscopy
description: An endoscopy of the small intestines accomplished while advancing the endoscope, which is assisted by one or two balloons

name: Laboratory Critical Values
description: Test results which deviate substantially from normal ranges of REFERENCE VALUES or other qualitative results. They trigger CLINICAL LABORATORY SERVICES to place a special alert to ensure PATIENT SAFETY.

name: Pharmacogenomic Testing
description: The detection of genetic variability (e.g., PHARMACOGENOMIC VARIANTS) relevant to PHARMACOGENETICS and PRECISION MEDICINE. The purpose of such genetic testing is to help determine the most effective treatment options and their optimum dosages with least potential risks for DRUG-RELATED SIDE EFFECTS AND ADVERSE REACTIONS.

name: Immunogenicity, Vaccine
description: The capacity of VACCINES to stimulate the ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSE to produce antibodies and antigen-specific T-CELL responses. It is typically measured in vaccinated individuals in observational studies setting.

name: Fasciotomy
description: Surgical incision on the FASCIA. It is used to decompress compartment pressure (e.g. in COMPARTMENT SYNDROMES; circumferential burns and extremity injuries) or to release contractures (e.g. in DUPUYTREN'S CONTRACTURE).

name: Stroke Rehabilitation
description: Restoration of functions to the maximum degree possible in a person or persons suffering from a stroke.

name: Barium Enema
description: X-RAY examination of LOWER GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT. Imaging is done while a BARIUM COMPOUND (e.g., BARIUM SULFATE) fills the large intestine via the rectum as a CONTRAST MATERIAL.

name: Blood Culture
description: Test to determine the presence of blood infection (e.g. SEPSIS; BACTEREMIA).

name: Prophylactic Mastectomy
description: Surgical removal of one or both breasts to prevent or reduce the risk of developing breast cancer in persons who may be predisposed.

name: Cardiac Rehabilitation
description: Restoration of functions to the maximum degree possible in a person or persons suffering from a CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. It also includes cardiac conditioning and SECONDARY PREVENTION in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk profile.

name: Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography
description: An imaging technique that combines a POSITRON-EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY (PET) scanner and a CT X RAY scanner. This establishes a precise anatomic localization in the same session.

name: Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography Computed Tomography
description: An imaging technique using a device which combines TOMOGRAPHY, EMISSION-COMPUTED, SINGLE-PHOTON and TOMOGRAPHY, X-RAY COMPUTED in the same session.

name: Computed Tomography Angiography
description: A non-invasive method that uses a CT scanner for capturing images of blood vessels and tissues. A CONTRAST MATERIAL is injected, which helps produce detailed images that aid in diagnosing VASCULAR DISEASES.

name: Shoulder Prosthesis
description: Replacement for a SHOULDER JOINT.

name: Arthroplasty, Replacement, Shoulder
description: Replacement of the SHOULDER JOINT.

name: Posterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction
description: Rebuilding of the POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT to restore functional stability of the knee.

name: Sustained Virologic Response
description: The continuous, long-term suppression of VIRAL LOAD, generally to undetectable levels, as the result of treatment with ANTIVIRAL AGENTS.

name: In Vivo Dosimetry
description: A procedure to measure the amount of radiation absorbed by the body during RADIOTHERAPY by DOSIMETERS in the patient’s skin or natural cavities.

name: Radiation Dosimeters
description: Devices that measure exposure to IONIZING RADIATION.

name: Donor Conception
description: Assisted reproductive techniques where eggs, sperm, both eggs and sperm (double donation), or embryos from donors are used.

name: Oxygen Radical Absorbance Capacity
description: A measure of the ability of a substance, such as a food, to quench oxygen free radicals in vitro.

name: Maximal Respiratory Pressures
description: A respiratory function test that includes the maximal inspiratory pressure and maximal expiratory pressure. It is determined by SPIROMETRY that measures the patient's RESIDUAL VOLUME and TOTAL LUNG CAPACITY and assesses the strength of RESPIRATORY MUSCLES.

name: Bathroom Equipment
description: Receptacles used for collection of human excrement.

name: Cannula
description: Short, hollow cylinders or tubes for insertion into a canal, vessel, or body cavity.

name: Patient Portals
description: A secure online website that provides patients convenient 24-hour access to personal health information via an Internet connection.

name: Gene Editing
description: Genetic engineering or molecular biology techniques that involve DNA REPAIR mechanisms for incorporating site-specific modifications into a cell's genome.

name: Conservative Treatment
description: Therapeutic approaches that are limited, gradual, or well-established as opposed to radical methods.

name: Single Molecule Imaging
description: High resolution imaging techniques that allow visualization of individual molecules of proteins, lipids, or nucleic acids within cells or tissues.

name: Slit Lamp Microscopy
description: A procedure that uses a SLIT LAMP to examine structures in the front of the EYE, such as the CONJUNCTIVA; CORNEA; IRIS; and AQUEOUS HUMOR.

name: Walking Speed
description: The rate at which steps are made while walking.

name: Simplified Acute Physiology Score
description: A severity of disease classification system designed to measure the severity of disease for patients aged 15 and over admitted to intensive care units.

name: Fitness Trackers
description: Devices used for measuring physical activity as an indication of HEALTH STATUS.

name: Integrative Oncology
description: These evidence-based therapies to reduce symptoms associated with treatment of cancer.

name: Patient Health Questionnaire
description: A self-administered version of the Primary Care Evaluation of Mental Disorders (PRIME-MD), a diagnostic tool containing modules on multiple mental health disorders including anxiety, alcohol, eating, and somatoform modules. The Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) is designed specifically for mood/depression scoring each of the 9 DSM-IV criteria based on the mood module from the original PRIME-MD. The Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7) scores 7 common anxiety symptoms.

name: Models, Spatial Interaction
description: Estimates of the flow of people, material or information between locations in geographic space.

name: Manual Lymphatic Drainage
description: The application of massage to control EDEMA and improve circulation by manually moving excess lymph out of a tissue.

name: Obesity Management
description: An integrated professional approach to screening, evaluation, control, and reduction of abnormal WEIGHT GAIN.

name: Whole Genome Sequencing
description: Techniques to determine the entire sequence of the GENOME of an organism or individual.

name: Exome Sequencing
description: Techniques used to determine the sequences of EXONS of an organism or individual.

name: Contraceptive Effectiveness
description: The rate of success or failure of a method of CONTRACEPTION; CONTRACEPTIVE AGENTS; or CONTRACEPTIVE DEVICES.

name: Diet, High-Protein
description: A diet that includes foods with a high protein content.

name: Dietary Approaches To Stop Hypertension
description: Dietary recommendations that promote reduction in or prevention of high blood pressure. Recommendations include increasing intake of fruits and vegetables, and high-fiber, low-fat foods and reducing the intake of DIETARY SODIUM and high fat foods.

name: Pre-Analytical Phase
description: Laboratory processes prior to specimen analysis. These processes include study design, compliance of the subjects investigated, compliance in adherence to protocols, choice of specimens utilized and sample collection.

name: Nonlinear Optical Microscopy
description: Microscopic imaging techniques that utilize nonlinear responses of light-matter interactions which occur with high-intensity illumination, such as from LASERS, and specialized light signal detection instrumentation to produce images without the need for dyes or fluorescent labels.

name: Second Harmonic Generation Microscopy
description: A microscopic imaging technique that takes advantage of the process of harmonic generation that occurs when photons interact to generate new photons of a different wavelength. In second harmonic generation, two photons of the same wavelength and frequency, such as from a LASER, interact inside a medium and are converted to a photon of twice the frequency and half of the wavelength of the two incident photons. The light signals captured are used to produce images that are dependent on the unique optical properties of the material.

name: Body Contouring
description: Plastic surgery to shape many areas of the body simultaneously. This may include LIPECTOMY or RHYTIDOPLASTY or both.

name: Scientific Experimental Error
description: Deviation or aberration in the practical implementation of standard empirical procedures, distinct from MEDICAL ERRORS and SCIENTIFIC MISCONDUCT.

name: Liquid Biopsy
description: Obtaining material for pathological examination and analysis, from bodily fluids. Material retrieved includes CELL-FREE NUCLEIC ACIDS; CELL-DERIVED MICROPARTICLES; EXOSOMES; CIRCULATING NEOPLASM CELLS; and other circulating cells and CELLULAR STRUCTURES.

name: Adverse Outcome Pathways
description: Models connecting initiating events at the cellular and molecular level to population-wide impacts. Computational models may be at levels relating toxicology to adverse effects.

name: Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs
description: Programs, usually run by state governments, that require pharmacists to collect and distribute data on the prescription and dispensation of CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES. They are intended to prevent the abuse of such substances by the patient, or their transfer to recreational users and drug dealers.

name: Anesthesia, Cardiac Procedures
description: A range of methods used to induce UNCONSCIOUSNESS; ANALGESIA; and MUSCLE RELAXATION during cardiac procedures.

name: Immunoturbidimetry
description: Immunochemical analysis which measures specific target antigen bound to antibody complex. Antibodies in assay form insoluble light scattering immune-aggregates which cause changes in the measured turbidity proportional to the concentration of the antigen.

name: Extracorporeal Shockwave Therapy
description: A nonsurgical treatment that uses either HIGH-ENERGY SHOCK WAVES or low energy ACOUSTIC WAVES to treat various musculoskeletal conditions (e.g., PLANTAR FASCIITIS; TENNIS ELBOW). A probe placed on the skin conducts the shock waves thereby delivering a mechanical force to the body’s tissues.

name: Bronchial Thermoplasty
description: Thermal destruction of the excess bronchial SMOOTH MUSCLE tissue with heat delivered through a catheter assembly attached to a BRONCHOSCOPE. It is often used to control BRONCHIAL HYPERREACTIVITY in severe ASTHMA for better AIRWAY MANAGEMENT.

name: Equivalence Trials as Topic
description: Works about trials that aim to show a new treatment is no better and no worse than the standard treatment.

name: Nicotine Chewing Gum
description: Chewing gum which contains NICOTINE.

name: Resonance Frequency Analysis
description: A non-invasive assessment of the stability of tissue-embedded prosthetic devices such as dental implants.

name: Preliminary Data
description: First-released version of study results in a series of data collection efforts used for the purpose of generating further interest in and or funding of a research study.

name: Mass Drug Administration
description: Administration of a medication to at-risk individuals in a population without individual diagnosis. It is often used in order to treat, control, and/or prevent spread of often endemic DISEASE OUTBREAKS such as NEGLECTED DISEASES in high disease burden areas.

name: Early Goal-Directed Therapy
description: Critical care treatment using intensive monitoring and aggressive management of perioperative hemodynamics in high risk patients,

name: Therapeutic Index, Drug
description: The ratio of the dose that produces toxicity to the dose that produces a clinically desired or effective response.

name: Synovectomy
description: Surgical removal of the SYNOVIAL MEMBRANE.

name: Meniscectomy
description: Surgical incision of a torn MENISCUS.

name: Mastoidectomy
description: Surgical removal of the diseased cells from the MASTOID PROCESS. It often involves simultaneous resection and/or repair of the MIDDLE EAR and EAR DRUM in MIDDLE EAR CHOLESTEATOMAS and MASTOIDITIS.

name: Keratectomy
description: Surgical excision of a part of the CORNEA.

name: Sphincterotomy
description: Surgical incision of a sphincter.

name: Myotomy
description: Surgical incision of the muscle.

name: Heller Myotomy
description: Surgical incision of the lower esophageal sphincter near the CARDIA often used to treat ESOPHAGEAL ACHALASIA.

name: Nephrolithotomy, Percutaneous
description: Surgical removal of large KIDNEY CALCULI by means of a percutaneous nephroscope which is passed into the KIDNEY PELVIS through a track created in the patient's back.

name: Nephrotomy
description: Surgical incision into any part of the kidney.

name: Nephroureterectomy
description: Surgical removal of a kidney and adjoining ureter.

name: Lateral Internal Sphincterotomy
description: Surgical incision of the INTERNAL ANAL SPHINCTER typically in the treatment of FISSURE IN ANO; chronic ANAL FISSURE and FECAL INCONTINENCE.

name: Hemodynamic Monitoring
description: Continuous measurement of the movement and forces of blood in the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM.

name: Salpingo-oophorectomy
description: Combined surgical resection of the fallopian tube and the ovary.

name: Pyloromyotomy
description: Surgical incision of the PYLORUS used to treat pyloric stenoses (e.g. INFANTILE HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS).

name: Vulvectomy
description: Surgical resection of the VULVA.

name: Amniotomy
description: A method of inducing labor by deliberate rupture of the AMNION to cause the release of amniotic fluid.

name: Abuse-Deterrent Formulations
description: Drug formulations or delivery systems intended to discourage the abuse of CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES. These may include physical barriers to prevent chewing or crushing the drug; chemical barriers that prevent extraction of psychoactive ingredients; agonist-antagonist combinations to reduce euphoria associated with abuse; aversion, where controlled substances are combined with others that will produce an unpleasant effect if the patient manipulates the dosage form or exceeds the recommended dose; delivery systems that are resistant to abuse such as implants; or combinations of these methods.

name: Contraindications
description: A condition or factor associated with a recipient that makes the use of a drug, procedure, or physical agent improper or inadvisable. Contraindications may be absolute (life threatening) or relative (higher risk of complications in which benefits may outweigh risks).

name: Contraindications, Drug
description: A condition or factor associated with a recipient that makes the use of a specific drug improper or inadvisable.

name: Contraindications, Procedure
description: A condition or factor associated with a recipient that makes the use of a procedure improper or inadvisable.

name: Gene Drive Technology
description: The techniques involved in creating and inserting synthetic selfish genetic elements called gene drives. Gene drives carry a payload gene and are designed to increase in frequency in the population over time, eventually to all members of the population.

name: Transplantation, Haploidentical
description: Transplantation between individuals who share a partial haplotype match.

name: Adaptive Clinical Trials as Topic
description: Works about clinical studies in which a prospectively planned opportunity is included to modify trial designs and hypotheses based on analysis of data from subjects in the study.

name: Long-Acting Reversible Contraception
description: Prevention of CONCEPTION by devices, chemical substances or agents with contraceptive activity in females which last for years and can be removed.

name: Prolotherapy
description: Treatment of MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN by injecting a substance into a joint space, ligament, or tendon to promote the growth of new tissue.

name: Multifocal Intraocular Lenses
description: Artificially implanted lenses that direct light toward distant and near focal points allowing clear vision for a range of distances.

name: Ion Mobility Spectrometry
description: Techniques for separation and identification of ionized molecules based on their drift through a gas phase after being accelerated by an electric field. Their mobilities will be effected by their shape, size, and charge.

name: Diet, High-Protein Low-Carbohydrate
description: A diet that consists mainly of foods with a high content of protein and limited amounts of CARBOHYDRATES.

name: Therapeutic Index
description: An indicator of the benefits and risks of treatment.

name: Patient Generated Health Data
description: Health-related data created, recorded, or gathered by patients, family members, or caregivers, to help address a health concern. Distinct from data generated in clinical settings and through encounters with providers.

name: Wearable Electronic Devices
description: Electronic implements worn on the body as an implant or as an accessory. Examples include wearable diagnostic devices, wearable ACTIVITY TRACKERS, wearable INFUSION PUMPS, wearable computing devices, SENSORY AIDS, and electronic pest repellents.

name: Retention in Care
description: Patient's regular engagement with medical care after initial entry into the system.

name: Endurance Training
description: Exercise programs of relatively long duration and moderate intensity, which enhance maximal oxygen uptake, increasing PHYSICAL STAMINA.

name: Ventilation-Perfusion Scan
description: A two-part radionuclide imaging that measures VENTILATION-PERFUSION RATIO of the lungs often used to investigate PULMONARY EMBOLISM. Image acquisitions may be performed using various combinations of gamma camera, PET and SPECT scanning techniques.

name: Drug Development
description: The entire process of bringing a new drug to the market. It includes both preclinical and clinical testing, and regulatory approval.

name: Negative Results
description: Subject matter related to research studies in which the data do not demonstrate any clear evidence of effect, especially if an effect was expected.

name: Pinealectomy
description: Surgical removal of the PINEAL GLAND including resection of pineal tumor (PINEALOMA) and CYSTS.

name: Gait Analysis
description: Determination of the level of functional limitation that may be due to pathology, and evaluating rehabilitative intervention of the way in which the body moves from one point to another. Most often, this is done by walking.

name: Latent Class Analysis
description: A statistical algorithm used to analyze clusters of observed variables by constructing categorical unobserved or latent segment based on weighted analysis and the average probabilities. Such latent classes are used to infer variables whose relationships are not directly observed. In biomedical research, it is often used to categorize data that allows the determination of symptom clusters.

name: Bone-Anchored Prosthesis
description: A prosthesis designed to attach directly to the bone via fixtures implanted into the bone rather than a socket.

name: Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma
description: Rapid bedside ultrasound examination performed by medical personnel (surgeons, emergency physicians, paramedics and others), as a screening test for blood around the heart (PERICARDIAL EFFUSION) or abdominal organs (HEMOPERITONEUM) after trauma.

name: Orthodontic Appliances, Fixed
description: ORTHODONTIC APPLIANCES attached to the teeth by adhesive material which cannot be removed from the mouth by the patient. These devices apply force to the teeth and supporting structures, thereby producing changes which control their growth and development.

name: Shared Governance, Nursing
description: Model of nursing practice with shared decision processes designed to integrate core values and beliefs that professional practice embraces, as a means of achieving quality care.

name: Plastination
description: Preservation technique in which epoxy polymers are used to preserve tissue or an organ resulting in anatomically authentic dry specimens often used in teaching of anatomy.

name: Lipoabdominoplasty
description: Aesthetic surgical treatment of the abdominal region using LIPOSUCTION associated with ABDOMINOPLASTY.

name: Progression-Free Survival
description: Length of time during and after the treatment of a disease, such as cancer, that a patient lives with the disease but the disease does not get worse.

name: Facilities and Services Utilization
description: Extent of use of facilities or services. It includes overuse and underuse.

name: Procedures and Techniques Utilization
description: Extent of use of procedures or techniques. It includes overuse and underuse.

name: Equipment and Supplies Utilization
description: Extent of use of equipment or supplies. It includes overuse and underuse.

name: Regenerative Endodontics
description: A dental specialty concerned with biologically-based procedures designed to physiologically replace damaged tooth structures, including dentin and root structures, as well as cells of the pulp-dentin complex.

name: Proctectomy
description: Surgical resection of the RECTUM.

name: Clinical Trials, Veterinary as Topic
description: Works about clinical studies in which animal participants are assigned to receive one or more interventions so that researchers can evaluate the interventions on biomedical or health-related outcomes. The assignments are determined by the study protocol. Animal participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions.

name: Radiofrequency Therapy
description: The use of RADIO WAVES to conduct therapeutic procedures. The specific frequency, dosage, and intensity used vary depending on the desired effects which include heating, electrical stimulation, or ablation of tissues.

name: Radiofrequency Ablation
description: Removal of tissue using heat generated from electrodes delivering an alternating electrical current in the frequency of RADIO WAVES.

name: Quantitative Light-Induced Fluorescence
description: A FLUORESCENCE technique used in DENTISTRY for the analysis of mineral changes in DENTAL ENAMEL to detect early DENTAL CARIES, or for the evaluation other normal or pathological processes or lesions of the dental enamel.

name: Tandem Affinity Purification
description: A technique used to isolate specific interacting partners of MACROMOLECULAR COMPLEXES that have been assembled with a tagged component (bait) that interacts with other partners in the complex. The interacting bait component is labeled with a dual-affinity tag that allows for capture of the complex by IMMUNOPRECIPITATION, followed by purification of only the partners of the complex interacting with the bait by affinity chromatography.

name: Maze Procedure
description: A surgical treatment in which heart tissue is scarred (cut-and-sew method), excised or otherwise destroyed in an open chest approach to direct electrical signals through a more controlled path via the ATRIOVENTRICULAR NODE. It is often used to restore normal rhythms in ATRIAL FIBRILLATION.

name: Shared Medical Appointments
description: Clinical encounters in which patients receive healthcare from one or more health professionals, in a group setting. These may include patient education and counseling, physical examination, and clinical support. Patients usually share a mutual attribute such as a medical condition.

name: Observational Studies, Veterinary as Topic
description: Works about clinical studies in which animal subjects may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions and where the investigator does not assign subjects to specific interventions.

name: Involuntary Commitment
description: Non-voluntary institutionalization or isolation following refusal or failure to take medication, to complete treatment, or to adhere to infection control precautions, or behavior that may or does endanger self or others.

name: Dry Needling
description: Intervention that uses a thin filiform needle to penetrate the skin and stimulate underlying myofascial trigger points, muscular, and connective tissues for the management of neuromusculoskeletal pain and movement impairments.

name: Genetic Introgression
description: The transfer of genetic material from one species to another by inter-species hybridization and repeated backcrossing.

name: Cell Encapsulation
description: The encapsulation of cells into semi-permeable microcapsules or MICROSPHERES that permits protection of encapsulated cells and allows passage of essential nutrients and release of a therapeutic product (e.g. INSULIN).

name: Sino-Nasal Outcome Test
description: Patient-reported measure of outcome in sino-nasal disorders such as rhinosinusitis and nasal polyposis.

name: Rapid Sequence Induction and Intubation
description: A method of maintaining airway patency and administering anesthesia during emergency situations when it cannot be determined if the patient is fasting or not; or in other instances where there is a risk of aspiration. The method includes a series of events that involve the administration of SEDATIVES to induce unconsciousness, followed by NEUROMUSCULAR BLOCK AGENTS to improve the intubating conditions, followed by endotracheal intubation.

name: Chronic Disease Indicators
description: A set of surveillance indicators of disease developed by consensus among the CDC, the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists, and the National Association of Chronic Disease Directors. It enables public health professionals and policymakers to retrieve uniformly defined state and selected metropolitan-level data for CHRONIC DISEASES and RISK FACTORS that impact public health.(https://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/data/index.htm)

name: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy
description: Procedures with continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration or perfusion) via vascular access designed to mimic kidney function in kidney diseases (e.g., ACUTE RENAL FAILURE and poisoning).

name: Wastewater-Based Epidemiological Monitoring
description: Sampling of the liquids generated from industrial processes, sanitary fixtures and appliances, food handling, etc., to collect and analyze epidemiological information (such as pathogen levels, or concentrations of pesticides, pharmaceuticals, or other substances) from metabolic excretion products, household liquid wastes, and industrial wastes.

name: Cupping Therapy
description: A traditional practice, most notably in traditional medicine, which involves placing cups on the skin to create suction believed to help increase blood flow and promote healing associated with chronic neck and low back pain in the short term (From National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, https://nccih.nih.gov/news/cupping (Accessed 11/5/2018)).

name: Intermittent Renal Replacement Therapy
description: Procedures with non-continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration and/or perfusion) via vascular access by increasing blood flow rate compared to CONTINUOUS RRT.

name: Hybrid Renal Replacement Therapy
description: Procedures involving non-continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration or perfusion) via vascular access with settings for dialysate and blood flow rates and treatment duration settings hybrid between CRRT TECHNIQUE and IRRT TECHNIQUE.

name: Hot Melt Extrusion Technology
description: Solvent-free method for preparing numerous types of drug delivery systems and dosage forms for active pharmaceutical ingredients that have solubility issues. It involves pumping polymeric materials at temperatures above their glass transition temperature to mix in active pharmaceutical ingredients with or without binders thus forming an amorphous product with an increase in the dissolution profile for the active pharmaceutical ingredients.

name: Early Warning Score
description: Tool for bedside evaluation based on five physiological parameters: SYSTOLIC PRESSURE, PULSE, RESPIRATORY RATE, BODY TEMPERATURE and AVPU (alert, voice, pain, unresponsive) score.

name: Hormonal Contraception
description: Contraceptive methods that utilize HORMONAL CONTRACEPTIVE AGENTS.

name: Hydrogen Deuterium Exchange-Mass Spectrometry
description: A mass spectrometry method utilizing hydrogen-deuterium exchange kinetics to study conformational and dynamic changes especially of proteins, such as interactions during ligand binding and allosteric effects during catalysis.

name: Cardio Ankle Vascular Index
description: An index of ARTERIAL STIFFNESS obtained from PULSE WAVE VELOCITY measurements between the heart and the ankle.

name: Smart Glasses
description: Computerized eyewear with multiple technological applications for advanced computing and interoperability. Smart glasses are optimized to facilitate information and data access, capture, display, transfer, and manipulation.

name: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery
description: A protocol of components related to preadmission, preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative care. The protocol is implemented with the goal of improving patient recovery, facilitating earlier discharge from the hospital, and potentially reducing health care costs without increasing complications or hospital readmissions. The protocol components may contribute to minimizing, and/or improving the response to, physiological stress associated with surgery.

name: Open Abdomen Techniques
description: Abdominal wound closure techniques in which the opening from a laparoscopic abdominal incision is left open, but covered, to reduce or prevent INTRA-ABDOMINAL HYPERTENSION.

name: Dual Anti-Platelet Therapy
description: Treatment with a combination of two types of antiplatelet agents to prevent blood clotting - usually ASPIRIN and another of the PLATELET AGGREGATION INHIBITORS.

name: Single-Case Studies as Topic
description: Trials that consider an individual patient as the sole unit of observation in a study investigating the efficacy or side-effects of different interventions to determine the optimal intervention for an individual patient using objective data-driven criteria.

name: Carotid-Femoral Pulse Wave Velocity
description: The transit time of an AORTIC PRESSURE wave between the COMMON CAROTID ARTERY and the COMMON FEMORAL ARTERY. It is a standard measure of ARTERIAL STIFFNESS.

name: Microwave Imaging
description: Use of MICROWAVES as a diagnostic tool.

name: Lymph Node Ratio
description: The ratio of metastatic to total examined LYMPH NODES.

name: Cell Line Authentication
description: Techniques used to characterize and confirm the identity of a CELL LINE. Characterization involves authentication to verify that it matches the original description of the cells and ensures that they are not cross-contaminated with another cell line. This is done to avoid attributing data incorrectly to the wrong cell line.

name: Noninvasive Prenatal Testing
description: The analysis of cell-free fetal DNA or the DNA from fetal cells that are biopsied from a pregnant woman’s blood, to screen for genetically-determined traits and genetic abnormalities.

name: Chromatin Immunoprecipitation Sequencing
description: A technique for identifying the BINDING SITES on nucleic acid sequences that are associated with binding proteins.

name: Hair Analysis
description: Examination of hair by chemical, physical, or microscopic means.

name: Duration of Therapy
description: Planned or actual duration of various treatments or preventive measures.

name: RNA-Seq
description: High-throughput nucleotide sequencing techniques developed for determining and analyzing the composition of the TRANSCRIPTOME of a sample.

name: Perfusion Index
description: The ratio of arterial blood flow (PULSATILE FLOW) to venous, capillary, and tissue blood flow (non-pulsatile blood flow) - as measured regionally or peripherally.

name: Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging
description: Magnetic Resonance Imaging technique that combines functional imaging techniques such as diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging and magnetic spectroscopy. This technique is widely used for active surveillance in prostate cancer imaging.

name: Nanopore Sequencing
description: A sequencing protocol that drives nucleic acids (DNA or RNA) in an electric field through NANOPORES allowing single molecule sequence analysis.

name: Clinical Decision Rules
description: Scores or algorithms that correlate with clinically significant findings and that are used to predict an outcome, or suggest a diagnostic or therapeutic action.

name: Hyperspectral Imaging
description: The use of SPECTROMETRY measurements (of radiance, reflectance, optical scattering, absorption, etc.) made for each point of an image, across the whole spectrum of a selected spectral range such as infrared, visual, ultraviolet, or X-rays. Hyperspectral images are analyzed to determine the make up and location of specific chemical compounds in the objects being imaged.

name: Laser Speckle Contrast Imaging
description: Two-dimensional imaging created from the quantification of the blurring of speckle (randomly varying intensity patterns of light seen after it is scattered through a medium) that occurs spatially or temporally. LSCI is used for measuring blood flow in tissues such as the retina, skin, and brain.

name: Mediation Analysis
description: A type of statistical analysis used to understand, clarify, and explain the relationship and pathway between a presumed cause (an independent variable) and effect (dependent variable) with respect to causal links (mediating variables) and/or to analyze the effect of an intervention (mediating factor/variable) on an outcome.

name: Diagnostic Reference Levels
description: Radiological values used as guides to indicate whether the radiation dosage or amount of radiopharmaceutical being given to a patient is unusually high or unusually low for the specific medical imaging procedure.

name: Sanitary Surveys, Water Supply
description: Review of public systems to assess their capability to supply safe drinking water. (From: https://www.epa.gov/dwreginfo/sanitary-surveys).

name: Preoperative Exercise
description: Various physical exercises implemented before a surgery designed for better TREATMENT OUTCOME.

name: Brain Cortical Thickness
description: Measurements of the thickness of the CEREBRAL CORTEX often detected automatically from medical imaging. Abnormal changes in cortical thickness (e.g., CORTICAL THINNING) are potential biomarkers for various neuropathologies.

name: Photothermal Therapy
description: Application of LOCAL HYPERTHERMIA within a specific tissue using electromagnetic radiation to convert light/laser into heat often coupled with PHOTOSENSITIZER including nanoparticle.

name: Heart Disease Risk Factors
description: Aspects of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inherited conditions and characteristics, which are determined to be associated with HEART DISEASES.

name: HIV Testing
description: Diagnosis of HIV INFECTIONS by assaying bodily fluids or tissues for the presence of HIV ANTIBODIES; HIV ANTIGENS; or the VIRAL RNA of HIV.

name: Analytic Hierarchy Process
description: A technique or tool used to analyze choices for complex decisions, by organizing them, for analysis, into a tree structure.

name: Cardiometabolic Risk Factors
description: A cluster of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inborn or inherited conditions and characteristics, which, on the basis of epidemiological evidence, is known to be associated with CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES and TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS.

name: Health Belief Model
description: A model which is based on certain predictors of a person’s perception of threat severity, susceptibility, interventional benefits and self-efficacy about a health threat that can be used to promote and educate health behavior.

name: Transtheoretical Model
description: A model which is based on a theory that people don’t change at once but instead rely on multiple stages of readiness to change. Each stage in turn is associated with strategies for progressing through that stage.

name: Mechanical Tests
description: Evaluation of mechanical properties of material or a device.

name: Multidimensional Scaling Analysis
description: A method of providing a visual representation of similarities among a set of data by plotting a map of perceived similarities on a set of vectors in p-dimensional space such that distances among them correspond to a function of the input matrix.

name: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy
description: A cancer treatment that involves filling the abdominal cavity with heated chemotherapy drugs. It is performed after the surgeon removes tumors or lesions from the abdominal area, to kill any cancer cells that remain after surgery and reduce the risk for cancer recurrence. (From: https://www.mdanderson.org/treatment-options/hyperthermic-intraperitoneal-chemotherapy.html; Feb, 20, 2020).

name: Eye-Tracking Technology
description: Technology used for EYE MOVEMENT MEASUREMENTS, which capture and measure a persons EYE MOVEMENT and/or EYE GAZE

name: Drug Tapering
description: Gradual discontinuation or reduction of a therapeutic dose of a particular drug over a period of time.

name: Nasoalveolar Molding
description: A presurgical facial orthotic treatment for patients with bilateral and unilateral CLEFT LIP and CLEFT PALATE. The treatment uses NASOALVEOLAR MOLDING DEVICES designed to reduce the cleft gap, reposition the alveolar segments to improve nasal symmetry, shaping and lessening the severity of the cleft deformity before primary palatoplasty, cheiloplasty, and RHINOPLASTY.

name: Glycemic Control
description: Strategies used for regulating BLOOD GLUCOSE levels. Such strategies include administration of INSULIN; DIETARY MODIFICATION; and EXERCISE.

name: Surgical Navigation Systems
description: Hardware and software tools that coordinate the use of imaging data (IMAGE INTERPRETATION, COMPUTER ASSISTED) to provide measurements for the planning of surgery and guidance of instruments during operating procedures in COMPUTER-ASSISTED SURGERY.

name: Self-Testing
description: Process whereby a person who wants to know his or her health status collects a specimen, performs a test and interprets the test result in private.

name: Treatment Switching
description: When patients in a randomized clinical trial switch from the treatment initially assigned to them to another treatment, typically from the control to experimental treatment.

name: Spray Drying
description: Method of drying liquids and liquid suspensions to prepare drugs in their final dehydrated powder form.

name: Models, Biopsychosocial
description: A systematic integration of biological, psychological, and social approaches to the study of mental health and specific mental disorders.

name: Clinical Reasoning
description: Process by which clinicians collect signs and process information to understand the patient's medical situation or problem, and then plan and implement appropriate medical interventions.

name: COVID-19 Testing
description: Diagnosis of COVID-19 by assaying bodily fluids or tissues for the presence of COVID-19 antibodies, SARS-COV-2 antigens or the VIRAL RNA of SARS-COV-2.

name: Automated Facial Recognition
description: Electronic identification of a human based on attributes of the face.

name: User-Centered Design
description: Design process using input from users regarding systems, devices, or software.

name: COVID-19 Nucleic Acid Testing
description: Diagnosis of COVID-19 by assaying bodily fluids or tissues for the presence of the VIRAL RNA of SARS-COV-2.

name: COVID-19 Serological Testing
description: Diagnosis of COVID-19 by assaying bodily fluids or tissues for the presence antibodies specific to SARS-COV-2 or its antigens.

name: N95 Respirators
description: Respiratory protective devices designed to achieve a close seal around the nose and mouth to maintain efficient filtration of aerosolized particles and droplets. They are often fitted for the prevention of the spread of infections (e.g. COVID19) or to administer inhaled anesthetics or other gases.

name: Vaccine Development
description: The entire process of introducing a new vaccine for use in VACCINATION including pre-clinical development, testing in CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIAL, manufacturing, approval/licensing and distribution.

name: Vaccine Efficacy
description: A measurement of disease risk reduction among vaccinated compared to unvaccinated persons under ideal conditions such as in a clinical trial. Such disease reduction measured under typical field conditions is vaccine effectiveness. In contrast vaccine potency is measured in an assay to ensure proper dosing and storage of vaccines whereas vaccine immunogenicity measures its ability to induce an immune response in a vaccinated individual in observational studies.

name: Healthy Life Expectancy
description: The expected number of remaining years of life spent in good health from a particular age, assuming current rates of mortality and morbidity.

name: Disability-Adjusted Life Years
description: It is the sum of years of life lost due to PREMATURE MORTALITY and the number of years lived with disability, due to disease or health condition in a population. This is a measurement of BURDEN OF DISEASE.

name: Umbilical Cord Clamping
description: Method of placing clamps on the UMBILICAL CORD before cutting after birth.

name: Cell Culture Techniques, Three Dimensional
description: Methods for growing cells in a way that they form three-dimensional shapes, such as on a three-dimensionally shaped substrate or as free-falling aggregates in stirred liquids.

name: Video-Assisted Techniques and Procedures
description: Techniques or procedures performed with visualization via video transmission.

name: Ex utero Intrapartum Treatment Procedures
description: Prenatal interventions to manage fetal anomalies or FETAL DISEASES ex utero while maintaining the uteroplacental circulation during obstetric delivery. EXIT procedures are divided into EXIT-to-airway; EXIT-to-ECMO; and EXIT-to-resection.

name: Overdiagnosis
description: The labeling of a person with a disease or abnormal condition that would not have caused the person harm if left undiscovered, creating new diagnoses by medicalizing ordinary life experiences, or expanding existing diagnoses by lowering thresholds or widening criteria without evidence of improved outcomes. Individuals derive no clinical benefit from overdiagnosis although they may experience physical, psychological or financial harm.

name: Anticoagulation Reversal
description: Treatment strategies used to manage bleeding events that occur during the use of ANTICOAGULANTS.

name: Aquatic Therapy
description: Physical therapy administered while the body is immersed in an aquatic environment.

name: Genomic Medicine
description: A medical discipline using genomic information about an individual as part of their clinical care (e.g. for diagnostic or therapeutic decision-making) and the health outcomes and policy implications of that clinical use. (From www.genome.gov/health/Genomics-and-Medicine accessed 12/28/2020)

name: Hospital to Home Transition
description: Patient-centered hospital discharge to home planning and transition.

name: Mirror Movement Therapy
description: Rehabilitation therapy in which a mirror is placed between the arms or legs so that the image of a moving non-affected limb gives the illusion of normal movement in the affected limb. This stimulates different brain regions for movement, sensation, and pain. (www.cochrane.org/CD008449 access 12/28/2020)

name: Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Testing
description: Test to measure the levels of NITRIC OXIDE (an ENDOTHELIUM-DEPENDENT RELAXING FACTOR) in the exhaled air. FeNO test is used to determine levels of inflammation in the pulmonary ENDOTHELIUM often associated with endothelium associated diseases, e.g., ASTHMA.

name: Canonical Correlation Analysis
description: Mathematical procedure that transforms vectors of variables into canonical variate pairs and finds their correlation to describe strength of association.

name: Cellular Automata
description: Space-oriented dynamic modeling ALGORITHMS acting in an array of cells, whose temporal states evolve based on the rules (algorithms) of the automata. They are used to model complex dynamic systems for study and analysis in a variety of scientific fields.

name: Myofascial Release Therapy
description: A massage therapy which focuses on releasing MUSCLE TIGHTNESS often used to relieve muscular pain from myofascial tissues (e.g., MYOFASCIAL PAIN SYNDROME).

name: Viral Pseudotyping
description: Technique in which endogenous ENVELOPE PROTEINS have been replaced by use of a chimeric vector. For instance a viral vector with SIMIAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS can be coated with the VIRAL ENVELOPE PROTEINS from Vesicular stomatitus virus. Use of these types of vectors are useful in developing NEUTRALIZATION TESTS by enabling infection of almost universal set of host cells.

name: Blood Flow Restriction Therapy
description: A technique which combines low intensity exercise with blood flow occlusion by use of a cuff. The cuff is placed close to the muscle being exercised thereby recreating a HYPOXIA to mimic the effects of high intensity exercise.

name: Ambulatory Care Sensitive Conditions
description: Various health conditions in OUTPATIENT CARE settings for which adequate management, treatment and interventions delivered in the ambulatory care setting could potentially prevent HOSPITALIZATION.

name: Epidemiological Models
description: Mathematical models of the transmission of infectious diseases. They predict spread of a disease by incorporating disease-related (e.g., infectious agent, mode of transmission, latent period, infectious period) and abiotic factors (e.g., social, cultural, demographic, and geographic factors).

name: Chemometrics
description: The use of statistical and mathematical methods to analyze chemical observations and phenomena, such as epidemiological analysis of spectroscopically identified bacteria or QUANTITATIVE STRUCTURE-ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIP.

name: Climate Models
description: Computer representations that simulate or predict the behavior or activity of WEATHER systems, processes, or phenomena.

name: Dacryocystography
description: An image guided examination of the NASOLACRIMAL APPARATUS including NASOLACRIMAL DUCT.

name: Digit Ratios
description: Ratio between lengths of fingers and/or toes that is sometimes characteristic of an exposure to ENDOCRINE DISRUPTORS during FETAL DEVELOPMENT.

name: Nanoparticle Drug Delivery System
description: Engineered NANOPARTICLES with unique physiochemical properties which improve drug BIOAVAILABILITY and site specific drug delivery.

name: Medicine, Iranian Traditional
description: Concepts of medicine and associated methods reflected in traditional Iranian medicine.

name: Census Tract
description: Small, relatively permanent statistical subdivisions of a county or equivalent entity that are updated by local participants prior to each decennial census as part of the U. S. Census Bureau's Participant Statistical Areas Program.(https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/about/glossary.html#par_textimage_13)

name: Network Pharmacology
description: A systems-based pharmacologic discovery process used to predict the multiple targets of multiple drugs in a complex mixture such as CHINESE HERBAL DRUGS. It involves analytical detection of chemicals plus prediction of pharmacologic activity and protein targets for each compound in the mixture and aggregating the net physiological effect.

name: Cognitive Training
description: A non-pharmacological form of treatment focusing on guided practice on tasks that target specific cognitive functions. These functions include memory, attention, and problem-solving. (from Cochrane.org/CD013069/DEMENTIA_cognitive-training-people-mild-moderate-dementia)

name: Information Motivation Behavioral Skills Model
description: A model for understanding patient behaviors, recognizes three constructs—information, motivation, and behavioral skills—needed to engage in a given health behavior, as specific individual determinants of behavior and behavioral change (Fisher & Fisher; Norton, 2009).

name: Rapid Diagnostic Tests
description: Diagnostic assays designed for use at the point-of-care (POC) that can be adapted for use in low-resource settings. These tests are low-cost, simple to operate and read, sensitive, specific, stable at high temperatures, and works in a short period of time.

name: Pharmacophore
description: A three-dimensional representation of a molecule that is used for modeling recognition of ligands and macromolecular targets.

name: Nerve Conduction Studies
description: Electrical tests to analyze the function of peripheral nerves by measuring various characteristics of NERVE CONDUCTION such as amplitude, velocity, and latency.

name: Dopaminergic Imaging
description: Functional brain imaging techniques that utilize various RADIONUCLIDE TRACERS that bind to different targets in the SYNAPSES of DOPAMINERGIC NEURONS.

name: Ultrasonography, Carotid Arteries
description: Ultrasound imaging of the CAROTID ARTERIES to measure their morphological components such as arterial wall shape and thickness; ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUE; and STENOSIS. BLOOD CIRCULATION in the carotid is visualized via DOPPLER ULTRASONOGRAPHY.

name: Single-Cell Gene Expression Analysis
description: Assaying the products of GENETIC TRANSCRIPTION in individual cells.

name: Clinical Relevance
description: Criteria to determine whether a finding (e.g., clinical examination, lab test, imaging results) requires a medical intervention for meaningful improvement in outcome often to avoid OVERDIAGNOSIS and/or OVERTREATMENT.

name: Motion Capture
description: Technological process of recording the MOTION and MOVEMENT of objects (e.g., surgical instrument in robotic surgery), body parts (e.g., EYE MOVEMENT), animals or people.

name: Electroporation Therapies
description: Treatment modalities that use pulsed electrical currents to permeabilize cell membranes and thereby enhance uptake of substances into cells of the body.

name: Irreversible Electroporation Therapy
description: The use of a dose of electricity that causes the pores that are formed in CELL MEMBRANES during ELECTROPORATION to remain open long enough to trigger CELL DEATH. It is sometimes used in conjunction with ELECTROCHEMOTHERAPY.

name: Tattoo Removal
description: Procedures to remove a tattoo. They may include laser surgery, excisional surgery, dermabrasion, or application of topical agents.

name: Theory of Planned Behavior
description: The construct in which intentions to perform behaviors of different kinds can be predicted with high accuracy from attitudes toward the behavior, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control; and these intentions, together with perceptions of behavioral control, account for considerable variance in actual behavior. (from Ajzen, Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, V.50, Issue 2, p.179-211.)

name: Motorized Mobility Scooter
description: A device ridden while seated that is typically propelled by an electric motor, and is used by those with limited or impaired mobility.

name: Bridge Therapy
description: Treatment used in a transition between former and new therapeutic regimes.

name: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel
description: A series of blood tests on one panel that measure the body's chemical balance and metabolism.

name: COVID-19 Drug Treatment
description: The use of DRUGS to treat COVID19 or its symptoms.

name: COVID-19 Serotherapy
description: Transfer of blood plasma derived from patients who have recovered from COVID-19 to non-immune hosts.

name: Phalloplasty
description: Surgery to restore, reconstruct, or improve the shape or appearance of a damaged, misshapen, or missing PENIS due to injury, disease, or developmental abnormalities.

name: Penile Transplantation
description: Surgical transference of the PENIS (or the PENIS and SCROTUM together) as a complete organ and the composite of many tissue types, from one individual to another.

name: Microphysiological Systems
description: Devices designed to recapitulate tissue or organ-level physiology and architect by combining MICROFLUIDICS; MICROFABRICATION; and 3D CELL CULTURE. Microphysiological systems mimic interconnections important in physiological or pathophysiological states of organ(s) and are often used for instance in HIGH THROUGHPUT SCREENING of drugs and factors important in disease modeling.

name: Local Field Potential Measurement
description: Recording of brain electrical activities recorded by a small-size electrode in the brain. It measures electric potential in the extracellular medium around neurons generated by small electric currents of local origin.

name: Obesity Paradox
description: An observation that high BODY MASS INDEX is sometimes associated with lower CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE mortality in certain population, e.g., ELDERLY.

name: Secondary Data Analysis
description: Analysis or reanalysis of existing data collected by someone else usually for a different purpose.

name: Volume Electron Microscopy
description: Electron microscopy techniques designed to reconstruct 3-D images at micrometer volume scales at nanometer (nm) level resolutions. Volume electron microscopy uses various techniques to render, segment and reconstruct 3-D images from stacked sequential 2-D images of incremental z-planes.

name: Transurethral Resection of Bladder
description: Surgical removal of tumor in the BLADDER with resectoscope inserted through the URETHRA.

name: Corneal Cross-Linking
description: An ophthalmic treatment used to prevent weakening or bulging of the CORNEA in corneal ECTASIA, e.g., post-LASIK ectasia, KERATOCONUS and pellucid marginal corneal degeneration. It uses UV-A and RIBOFLAVIN to crosslink and strengthen COLLAGEN fibers within the cornea.

name: Ribosome Profiling
description: A technique of mRNA sequence analysis that is used to determine which mRNAs are being actively translated. This technique relies on sequencing of RIBOSOME protected mRNA fragments (so-called ribosomal footprints) allowing the indication of the exact positions of ribosomes on transcripts.

name: Capillary Isoelectric Focusing
description: Isoelectric focusing in capillary gels instead of slab gels. Capillary gel electrophoresis generally allows higher resolution, higher detection sensitivity and easier integration with other separation and detection techniques.

name: Olfactory Training
description: A non-surgical and non-pharmacological exercise treatment designed to manage OLFACTORY DISORDERS.

name: Endovascular Aneurysm Repair
description: A minimally invasive surgical technique to repair aneurysms through the lumen of a blood vessel.

name: Blood Banking
description: The administrative procedures and methods required for collecting, characterizing and storing blood or plasma in BLOOD BANKS.

name: Urinary Sediment Analysis
description: Microscopic visualization and/or chemical analysis of the sediments in URINE.

name: Anticoagulation Bridge
description: A peri-operative bridge therapy procedure in patients with high risk THROMBOEMBOLIC events and the risk of bleeding.

name: Pathologic Complete Response
description: The disappearance of all signs of a disease upon REMISSION INDUCTION as supported by pathological examination.

name: Nicotine Replacement Therapy
description: Replacing NICOTINE from TOBACCO with an alternate source in order to reduce the severity of tobacco withdrawal during TOBACCO USE CESSATION.

name: Magnetic Resonance Myelography
description: A modified magnetic resonance imaging method for generating myelogram like images, characterized by high signal intensity of the CEREBROSPINAL FLUID, which permits visualization of spinal subarachnoid spaces and nerve root sheaths.

name: Diet, Plant-Based
description: A diet that emphasizes consumption of plant foods, such as grains, fruits, vegetables, nuts, and LEGUMES while reducing intake of animal-based foods.

name: Continuous Glucose Monitoring
description: GLUCOSE MONITORING that measures interstitial glucose concentration continuously throughout the entire day and night. It does not replace traditional HOME BLOOD GLUCOSE MONITORING.

name: Oral Frenectomy
description: Surgical procedures to release or remove abnormally short or tightly attached frenum (e.g., LINGUAL FRENUM or LABIAL FRENUM) associated with a pathological condition (e.g., TONGUE TIE and lip tie).

name: Symptom Burden
description: The subjective, quantifiable prevalence, frequency, and severity of symptoms placing a physiologic burden on patients and producing multiple negative, physical, and emotional patient responses.

name: Post-Exercise Recovery Techniques
description: Therapeutic modalities following a bout of exercise to reduce markers of muscle damage, soreness, fatigue, and inflammation.

name: Treatment Delay
description: A longer or slower than expected, or desired, amount of time between onset of symptoms and initiation of therapy.

name: Medicine, Thai Traditional
description: A system of traditional medicine which is based on the beliefs and practices of the Thai culture.

name: Maggot Debridement Therapy
description: Medical use of live MAGGOTS for cleaning non-healing wounds.

name: Non-Medical Prescribing
description: Prescribing by a healthcare professional other than a doctor or dentist.

name: Genetic Risk Score
description: Estimate of an individual's genetic liability to a trait or disease, calculated according to their genotype profile and relevant genome-wide association study data. (from Tutorial: a guide to performing polygenic risk score analyses. Nat Protoc. 2020 Sep;15(9):2759.)

name: Overlapping Surgery
description: SURGICAL PROCEDURES performed on two or more patients that overlap in their start and finish times, but the critical portions or those activities which require the skill and expertise of the primary surgeon do not overlap. The primary surgeon initiates and participates in another operation when the surgeon has completed the critical portions of the first procedure and is no longer an essential participant in the final phase of the first operation.

name: Nanovaccines
description: Vaccines that use NANOPARTICLES as carriers and IMMUNOLOGIC ADJUVANTS.

name: Fluoride Treatment
description: The topical application of fluorides, usually in pastes, gels, varnishes, TOOTHPASTES or MOUTHWASHES, to reduce the incidence of DENTAL CARIES. Fluoride Treatment may occur in the dental office or at home. (https://jada.ada.org/article/S0002-8177(14)62166-8/fulltext)

name: Radiomics
description: Extraction of a large number of features from patient images using data characterization algorithms to uncover tumoral patterns and characteristics that improve diagnosis.

name: Percutaneous Collagen Induction
description: An alternative treatment for skin dysfunctions that stimulates COLLAGEN production by encouraging normal WOUND HEALING that occurs after any trauma by inducing microlesions.

name: Left Atrial Appendage Closure
description: A procedure that blocks the left ATRIAL APPENDAGE to reduce the risk of MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION associated with ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (AF). The left atrial appendage is often the site of BLOOD CLOT formation in AF.

name: Puberty Suppression
description: A non-intensive, reversible medical intervention achieved by using compounds that mimic the actions of GONADOTROPIN-RELEASING HORMONE (GnRH), which in turn slows or stops the physical changes associated with puberty such as the development of breasts or facial hair.

name: Forensic Imaging
description: The use of various imaging and image enhancement techniques in forensic investigative disciplines. It often includes FORENSIC MEDICINE platforms such as X-RAYS; CT XRAY; and MRI.

name: Intracameral Injection
description: A medical procedure in which medication is delivered directly into the ANTERIOR CHAMBER of the eye.

name: Elastin-Like Polypeptides
description: Synthetic biopolymers that are formed by repeating amino acid sequences that are naturally found in TROPOELASTIN. They are useful for various purposes, including DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS, TISSUE SCAFFOLDS, and ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS.

name: Neuroanesthesia
description: Anesthesia method that deals with the complexities of the physiology and pharmacology of the nervous system when providing anesthesia for patients undergoing neurological procedures.

name: Geriatric Anesthesia
description: Conducting anesthesia procedures in AGED adults, typically those aged 65 years and older.

name: Pediatric Anesthesia
description: Conducting anesthesia procedures in infants, children, and adolescents.

name: Postmortem Imaging
description: The generation of images of the body's structures, organs, and tissues after death.

name: Quantitative Phase Imaging
description: Contrast imaging generated from the measurements of phase shift changes of light waves as they pass through transparent objects of varying thickness and refractivity.

name: Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry
description: A microanalytical technique combining mass spectrometry and liquid chromatography for the qualitative as well as quantitative determinations of compounds.

name: Pooled Testing
description: Mixing of several samples together in a batch or pooled sample, then testing the pooled sample with a diagnostic test. This approach increases the number of individuals that can be tested using the same amount of resources.(CDRH-EUA-Templates@fda.hhs.gov)

name: Human Challenge Trials as Topic
description: Works about trials in which participants are intentionally challenged (whether or not they have been vaccinated) with exposure to an infectious disease organism.

name: Dimensionality Reduction
description: A machine learning process used to reduce the number of attributes or features of data (called dimensionality) thereby simplifying understanding of the dataset without a loss in data integrity.

name: Hidden Markov Models
description: Finite learnable stochastic models often used in MACHINE LEARNING consisting of two processes: a MARKOV CHAIN and an event observed and analyzed in a state unknown or hidden to the observer. Hidden Markov Models are often used in BIOINFORMATICS, time series analysis and speech and handwriting recognition.

name: Constraint Induced Movement Therapy
description: Rehabilitation treatment following an ischemic stroke where patients suffer from muscular weakness or paralysis on one side.It is also used as a therapy for children with cerebral palsy.

name: Tracheostomy Decannulation
description: Removal of the TRACHEOSTOMY tube.

name: Device Lead Extraction
description: Removal of electronic wire lead(s) of IMPLANTED ELECTRODES, e.g., implanted ARTIFICIAL PACEMAKER or IMPLANTABLE CARDIOVERTER DEFIBRILLATOR.

name: Hardware Removal
description: Surgical removal of devices, including BONE SCREWS, pins, BONE PLATES, and wires used in FRACTURE FIXATION. Hardwares in general refer to non-electrical devices, most often orthopedic, and are removed due to infection, malfunction and to allow proper growth.

name: Dynamic Contrast Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging
description: A non-invasive technique for measuring changes within the tumor MICROVASCULATURE.

name: Shotgun Sequencing
description: A laboratory technique for determining the DNA sequence of an organism's genome. In this approach, DNA of an organism is randomly broken into small DNA fragments which are then sequenced individually. Computational methods are then utilized to reassemble these sequenced fragments accurately, reconstructing the complete genome sequence.

name: Perfusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging
description: A specialized type of MRI technique that provides information about HEMODYNAMIC parameters such as CEREBRAL BLOOD VOLUME, CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW, and transit time. In perfusion MRI, an exogenous CONTRAST AGENT is usually injected to provide superior tissue contrast and easy delineation of perfusion abnormalities. Endogenous markers can also be used.

name: Aquablation
description: A minimally invasive water ablation procedure used for treating BENIGN PROSTATE HYPERPLASIA. During this procedure, a robotically controlled water jet is used to remove excess prostate tissue.

name: Onco-anesthesia
description: Methods used by specialized onco-anesthesiologists in the perioperative care of patients undergoing cancer-related diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The aim is to minimize preoperative complications, expedite recovery, and facilitate early return to intended oncological treatment.

name: Chemogenetics
description: The use of engineered small molecules to manipulate the activity of specific cells within living organisms, typically. Chemogenetic techniques are often used to study specific neural activity through genetically engineered receptors that bind specific endogenous or exogenous ligands.

name: Epigenome Editing
description: A genetic engineering technique that involves manipulating the EPIGENOME at the target region with minimal or no modification of the genomic DNA.

name: Pregnancy-Related Death
description: Death of a pregnant or birthing person during pregnancy or up to one year after the end of pregnancy from health issues related to pregnancy.

name: Treatment Expectations
description: Outcome anticipated or expected due to various qualities of a healthcare treatment.

name: Continuous Flow Chemistry
description: A process where chemical reactions are carried out in a continuously flowing stream rather than in batch production.

name: Forest Therapy
description: Sitting or walking in a FOREST or forested area and taking in all of the environmental stimuli of the forest - the sounds, images, atmospheric conditions, etc. as a form of therapy.

name: Portable X-Ray
description: A portable imaging device used to perform radiographic examinations outside the traditional radiology department. Mobile X-ray machines provide diagnostic imaging when patients cannot be easily moved or in locations that lack permanent imaging facilities.

name: Colorectal Surgical Procedures
description: Surgeries on the the COLON; RECTUM; and ANAL CANAL.

name: Microneedle Drug Delivery
description: A technique for delivering therapeutic compounds into the body through the skin with minimal invasiveness.

name: Surrogacy
description: A reproductive process where a SURROGATE MOTHER carries and gives birth to a child for another person or couple.

name: Lip Augmentation
