description: Ongoing collection, analysis, and interpretation of ecological data that is used to assess changes in the components, processes, and overall condition and functioning of an ECOSYSTEM.

name: Sagittal Abdominal Diameter
description: The height of the ABDOMEN as measured in the SUPINE POSITION.

name: Microscopy, Electrochemical, Scanning
description: A scanning probe microscopy technique that uses an ultramicroelectrode as the scanning probe that simultaneously records changes in electrochemical potential as it scans thereby creating topographical images with localized electrochemical information.

name: Olfactometry
description: Procedures for measuring a response to odorants.

name: Cool-Down Exercise
description: Tapering-off physical activity from vigorous to light, to gradually return the body to pre-exercise condition and metabolic state.

name: Metabolic Flux Analysis
description: Measurement of cells' substrate utilization and biosynthetic output for modeling of METABOLIC NETWORKS.

name: Posterior Capsulotomy
description: Procedures performed to remove CAPSULE OPACIFICATION that develops on the POSTERIOR CAPSULE OF THE LENS following removal of a primary CATARACT.

name: Alveolar Bone Grafting
description: Surgical procedure to add bone to the ALVEOLAR RIDGE in children born with a CLEFT LIP and a CLEFT PALATE.

name: Therapy, Soft Tissue
description: The assessment, treatment, and management of soft tissue injury or dysfunction. Therapy is designed to reduce tension and irritation in affected tissues and may include MASSAGE; muscle stretching, or direct pressure on muscles, connective tissue, and TRIGGER POINTS.

name: Pragmatic Clinical Trials as Topic
description: Works about clinical studies designed to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions in real-world health system practice.

name: Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring
description: The systematic checking of the condition and function of a patient's CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM during the course of a surgical operation.

name: Polypharmacology
description: The design or use of pharmaceutical agents that act on multiple targets or disease pathways.

name: Myocutaneous Flap
description: A mass of tissue, including skin and muscle, that has been cut away from surrounding areas for transplantation.

name: Multimodal Imaging
description: The use of combination of imaging techniques or platforms (e.g., MRI SCAN and PET SCAN) encompassing aspects of anatomical, functional, or molecular imaging methods.

name: Patient Care Bundles
description: Small sets of evidence-based interventions for a defined patient population and care setting.

name: Observational Studies as Topic
description: Works about clinical studies in which participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions, but the investigator does not assign participants to specific interventions (as in an interventional study).

name: Qigong
description: An ancient Chinese system of postures, exercises, breathing techniques, and meditations designed to improve and enhance the body's QI.

name: Neurophysiological Monitoring
description: The systematic checking of the condition and function of a patient's CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM during disease periods or following injuries, using various NEUROLOGICAL DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUES.

name: Cell- and Tissue-Based Therapy
description: Therapies that involve the TRANSPLANTATION of CELLS or TISSUES developed for the purpose of restoring the function of diseased or dysfunctional cells or tissues.

name: Papanicolaou Test
description: Cytological preparation of cells collected from a mucosal surface and stained with Papanicolaou stain.

name: Bioprospecting
description: The systematic search and discovery of natural substances which may have potential commercial applications.

name: Interrupted Time Series Analysis
description: A study that uses observations at multiple time points before and after an intervention (the interruption), in an attempt to detect whether the intervention has had an effect significantly greater than any underlying trend over time.

name: Controlled Before-After Studies
description: A study in which observations are made before and after an intervention, both in a group that receives the intervention and in a control group that does not.

name: Non-Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic
description: Works about a study where participants are assigned to a treatment, procedure, or intervention by methods that are not random. Non-randomized clinical trials are sometimes referred to as quasi-experimental clinical trials or non-equivalent control group designs.

name: Prophylactic Surgical Procedures
description: Surgical procedures done to prevent or reduce the risk of developing cancer or other disease conditions in persons who may be predisposed to such conditions.

name: Robotic Surgical Procedures
description: Surgical procedures performed remotely using a computer that controls surgical instruments attached to mechanical arms designed to perform the tasks of the surgeon.

name: Pedicle Screws
description: BONE SCREWS to be used in the pedicle of the vertebral arch.

name: Historically Controlled Study
description: A study that compares a group of participants receiving an intervention with a similar group from the past who did not.

name: Laminoplasty
description: A surgical procedure performed on selected pairs of vertebral lamina to relieve pressure on the SPINAL CORD and which also allows for osteoplastic enlargement of the SPINAL CANAL.

name: Cytoreduction Surgical Procedures
description: Operative procedures carried out to reduce a mass of tissue, for example, to reduce the total amount of tissue composing a tumor.

name: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
description: An endovascular procedure for the treatment of severe AORTIC VALVE STENOSIS. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is used as an alternative option in patients who are deemed at high risk or inoperable for traditional open-heart surgery.

name: Vascular Closure Devices
description: Products used to seal the openings in BLOOD VESSELS from incisions or punctures made during ENDOVASCULAR PROCEDURES.

name: Diving Reflex
description: BREATH HOLDING; VASOCONSTRICTION; and a drop in HEART RATE in response to submersion of the face in cold water.

name: Acetabuloplasty
description: Surgical reconstruction of the ACETABULUM.

name: Brachial Plexus Block
description: A blocking of NEURAL CONDUCTION in the network of nerve fibers innervating the UPPER EXTREMITY.

name: Gamma Rhythm
description: Brain waves characterized by a relatively high voltage or amplitude and a frequency of approximately 30-100 Hz. They are primarily observed during network engagement and sensory processing activities, during both waking and sleeping states.

name: Protective Factors
description: An aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, or inborn or inherited characteristic, which, on the basis of epidemiologic evidence, is known to be associated with prevention or mitigation of a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

name: Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation
description: A technique of brain electric stimulation therapy which uses constant, low current delivered via ELECTRODES placed on various locations on the scalp.

name: Waist-Height Ratio
description: The ratio of WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE to BODY HEIGHT.

name: Cervical Plexus Block
description: A blocking of NEURAL CONDUCTION in the network of nerve fibers innervating the neck and shoulder.

name: Diet, Paleolithic
description: A nutritional plan based on the presumed diet of pre-agricultural human ancestors. It consists mainly of MEAT, EGGS, NUTS, roots and fresh VEGETABLES and FRUITS, and excludes GRAIN, LEGUMES, DAIRY PRODUCTS, and refined DIETARY SUGARS.

name: Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors
description: An internationally recognized set of published rules used for evaluation of cancer treatment that define when tumors found in cancer patients improve, worsen, or remain stable during treatment. These criteria are based specifically on the response of the tumor(s) to treatment, and not on the overall health status of the patient resulting from treatment.

name: Slit Lamp
description: A microscope with a light source that can be projected into a linear beam. It allows cross-sectional viewing of the AQUEOUS HUMOR; CONJUNCTEIVA; CORNEA; EYELIDS; IRIS; and lens (see LENS, EYE) of the eye.

name: Patient-Specific Modeling
description: The development and application of computational models of human pathophysiology that are individualized to patient-specific data.

name: Fluorine-19 Magnetic Resonance Imaging
description: Magnetic resonance imaging diagnostic technique which uses fluorine-19 perfluorocarbon probes and contrast agents for high resolution image detection and quantitation.

name: Bioresonance Therapy
description: A form of holistic medicine in which ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES are used to diagnose and treat human and animal illness via manipulation of endogenous electromagnetic oscillations corresponding to the patient's current physiological condition.

name: Carbon-13 Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
description: Magnetic resonance spectroscopy involving detection of changes in the resonance of carbon-13 nuclei in organic molecules.

name: Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
description: Spectroscopy technique which measures changes in organic compounds by tracking the spectral energy of absorption of HYDROGEN atoms.

name: Subtractive Hybridization Techniques
description: Methods of studying differential GENE EXPRESSION of especially low-abundance, tissue-specific gene transcripts.

name: Axillofemoral Bypass Grafting
description: An extra-anatomic method of surgical revascularization in which the AXILLARY ARTERY is anastomosed to FEMORAL ARTERY.

name: Datasets as Topic
description: Subject matter related to the curation of data from research projects, stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

name: Health Information Exchange
description: Organizational framework for the dissemination of electronic healthcare information or clinical data, across health-related institutions and systems. Its overall purpose is to enhance PATIENT CARE.

name: In Vitro Techniques
